scope: Proposition 7.1 (Separated stages) of the manuscript “Directional transience implies ballisticity” (preprints/Directional-transience-implies-ballisticity-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 220 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8b305d1fbb11b2a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 42. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are fixed constants f, g, χ, K > 0 and an integer k ≥ 2 with 1 g < β 64 , (1 + f/g)D0 K < β 64 , having the following property. For every sufficiently large fixed b, put B = kb and choose a sufficiently large fixed floor sfl. At every level-count scale s ≥ sfl, put s− = se−fb , s+ = segb , He = ⌊se−b ⌋, H = ⌊seχb ⌋. For every probability π on k-tuples supported on {sep ≥ rs}, a fresh product environment satisfies Γπ h{sep(endpoints) ≥ rs− } ≥ e−B (1 ≤ h ≤ H), Γπ H{sep(endpoints) ≥ rs+ } ≥ e−B (35) with probability at least 1 − e−2Kb. Each test uses the full kernel from the same stage base; a passing test does not restrict the paths used by later tests.
